The difference between a questionnaire and a decision record

Proofline editorial · 14 November 2026 · 4 min read

A useful review record helps the next person understand the situation without reconstructing the entire conversation.

Start with the operating context.

A review desk for vendor security questionnaires. Track the open evidence request, the review owner and the decision that follows. The goal is to make a small number of important facts easy to find: the record reference, the location, the person responsible and the unresolved question.

The outstanding question belongs beside the evidence request and the person making the assessment. A table only becomes a workflow when someone can tell what needs attention and what the next step should be.

Give every open question an owner.

An open question needs a named person and a practical follow-up. A sample priority score can help sort a queue, but it cannot replace the judgment of the team responsible for the work.

Keep supplier security reviews moving from evidence request to decision.

A short checklist for the handover.

  1. Use a stable reference for each review.
  2. Record the relevant location and operational context.
  3. Explain the outstanding question in plain language.
  4. Name the person who will take the next step.
  5. Record the outcome before closing the item.

Keep the register useful.

Review open reviews regularly. A record that no one updates becomes another place to look, rather than a shared account of the work. Make the review part of a real team rhythm and keep the fields short enough for people to maintain.

The Proofline demonstration lets you try that sequence with illustrative records. Search the register, open a detail panel, add a note and record the next action. The demo data is not a report of actual customer operations.
